correctness.rationale: The vector field is globally Lipschitz. The (y,z) linear subsystem is Hurwitz with bounded forcing; the displayed quadratic Lyapunov part has determinant a+h(b−h)>0 in the strict regime, and its critical sum-of-squares form has compact sublevels on the positional cylinder. At equality put S=z+by/a, W=y−c sin(dx); then S′=−W and W′=aS−b(1+cos(dx))y, which together with the cosine potential gives E′=−b(1+cos(dx))y². On an invariant trajectory of zero dissipation, a nonzero y would force constant x on an interval, so y, z, and sin(dx) must vanish. LaSalle and connectedness select one of two equilibrium phases; continuity confines the late-time lift to one component of the inverse image of a small phase interval. At each even plane E≥2c², so a strictly lower initial energy prevents hitting either plane and even excludes those boundary equilibria as limits. Below threshold the Routh signs give one unstable eigenvalue at even equilibria and two at odd ones. Substitution of iω allows a nonzero imaginary root only at b=cd for odd parity; hence the strict subthreshold equilibria are hyperbolic. Their global stable manifolds are lower dimensional, and their countable union is null. The verification note and supporting Python were inspected, not executed; the finite tests are not needed for these conclusions.
